inline_text: ### Project Name meshllm ### Project Description A majority of the worlds compute capacity resides in distributed form, consumer devices (edge), isolated boxes/servers and even GPUs (and increasingly data centers). This can be utilised more effectively for AI workloads, in particular LLMs where the standard apis make consumption easier, it also makes provision of compute approachable as the workloads are "safer" to host then arbitrary cloud workloads. The benefit being more choice of hosting, self hosting and sharing of compute where it may otherwise be a sunk cost, underutilised. Meshllm is a project to allow people to pool compute (all hardware and operating system platforms) in a safe way so that it can be consumed via a standard api from standard and familiar tools (chat, harnesses, apps and more), making use of this hardware. ### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known) None ### Alignment with AAIF Mission meshllm matches with the aaif mission very well: * agentic workloads require LLM (and similar) apis to power harnesses (which meshllm provides) * opensource innovation to allow more to access and try LLMs, decision models and more * embraces open standards and protocols for inference, decisions, co-ordination (makes use of MCP, ACP and more) and could benefit from helping define more open standards for model hosting, observability, metering and more. Makes use of openresponses (and benefits from more open standards as they emerge) ### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects * started adjacent to the goose (AAIF) project to allow project members to share capacity with those who may not have ability to host models and curious (and built with block, an aaif member) * makes use of openresponses (infact an open api is critical to adoption) * makes use of MCP, skills (skills and MCP are a way in which subagents powered by mesh can be consumed ideally) Future synergies: * as it provides models (and routing) could work with agentgateway as a standard way for consumers to use it * opensandbox could be an interesting additional workload for pooling ### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption buzz.xyz embeds meshllm as an SDK allowing community members to share compute to power agents alongside cloud models meshchat.cloud and meshllm.cloud provide best efforts sharing via the community early stage project, around 100K monthly unique visitors to meshllm.cloud 4.1K stars on github, steadily climbing 150K downloads (github artifacts) corporate contributions from developers and end users: ### Technical Committee Sponsor (if identified) _No response_ ### GitHub Repository URL https://github.com/mesh-llm/mesh-llm ### License Apache 2.0 ### Governance Model Current governance involves a rotating set of core members who have high agency to effect change. This is a project which has grown up agent native to the velocity of change and turnover is expected to be high and embraced. Changes other than procedural do require human sign off from a member of core. Weekly technical/roadmap meetings are conducted via a video call async communications largely via buzz, some discord and github issues. This is evolving and still an early stage project. ### CI/CD & Release Workflow github actions bi-monthly release as needed .x patch versions are provided for critical fixes CI is on all PRs, including forks, which cover it across the the core platforms. Core platform support is important as it is hardware dependent, CUDA, ROCm, Vulcan, Metal etc and across matrix of operating systems and CPU/binary architectures (which means a large combination of GPU x CPU x OS). CD we produce "runtime" binaries for each permutation, and then one core mesh-llm monolithic binary for each OS/CPU combination (it will then fetch the appropriate GPU runtime). There are several plugin repositories which also have their own publish lifecycle, async from the core mesh-llm repo which can be installed/fetch into a given mesh-llm installation. CD also publishes some SDK assets to repositories for API consumption. ### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications https://github.com/Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md also make heavy use of specifications in the repo/design docs. AGENTS.md and skills in the repo provide peoples agents with detailed and in some cases enforced guidelines for this. ### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker https://github.com/Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm/issues ### External Project Dependencies is a rust project, kep dependencty is llama.cpp from huggingface (MIT) - here is a summary report but non exhuastive: # mesh-llm external dependencies Snapshot from 2026-11-17, `Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm`. ## Numbers | Measure | Count | |---|---| | Direct third-party dependencies of the `mesh-llm` package | 7 (`anyhow`, `clap`, `reqwest`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `tokio`, `urlencoding`) | | Third-party crates in the `mesh-llm` dependency tree, transitive | 536 | | Packages in `Cargo.lock` across the whole workspace | 1,072 | ## Key dependencies and licenses | Dependency | Role | License | |---|---|---| | llama.cpp (pinned `8954f194`, patched) | Inference engine | MIT | | iroh | Peer-to-peer QUIC transport | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | | tokio | Async runtime | MIT | | reqwest, axum, tonic | HTTP / gRPC | MIT (reqwest: MIT OR Apache-2.0) | | serde, clap | Serialization, command line | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | | tokenizers, safetensors, hf-xet | Hugging Face models | Apache-2.0 | | rustls, ring, aws-lc-rs | TLS / crypto | ISC and Apache-2.0 combinations | | ed25519-dalek | Signing | BSD-3-Clause | | nostr-sdk | Mesh discovery | MIT | | rusqlite | SQLite | MIT | | opentelemetry, prost, rmcp | Telemetry, protobuf, MCP | Apache-2.0 | | CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal | GPU backends | Vendor licenses | ## License summary (536 crates) - About 283 offer MIT or Apache-2.0, 120 are MIT only, and 24 are Apache-2.0 only. - No GPL, LGPL or AGPL licenses. No crate is missing a license field. These come from the license field in each crate's `Cargo.toml` (via `cargo metadata`), not from scanning license files. ## How to extract dependencies Run these from the repository root. ```bash # Direct dependencies of mesh-llm cargo tree -p mesh-llm --depth 1 # Full dependency tree cargo tree -p mesh-llm # Find out why a crate is included cargo tree -p mesh-llm -i # Every crate with version and license, as a CSV cargo metadata --format-version 1 \ | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.source) | [.name, .version, .license] | @csv' > deps.csv ``` ### Maintainers & Contributors Available in detail on github -but here is a summary with some affiliations mapped: Maintainers; | Name | GitHub | Affiliation | |---|---|---| | James Dumay | @i386 | General Inference | | Michael Neale | @michaelneale / @micspiral | Spiral (Block) | | Nick DiZazzo | @ndizazzo | tetrate | | Daniel Winter-Wijntjes | @danielwinterw | General Inference | | Steven Mih | @StevenMih | Action State Group | | Virgile Pourchet | @Virgile-pct | | | Ivan Golovach | @IvGolovach | | | Ben Carman | @benthecarman | Spiral (Block) | More contributors: | Martin Kleinberger | @kleinbem | | | thesvn | @iamthesvn | | | Ethan Zhang | @ethanyzhang | Action State Group | | Andrew Barnes | @Bortlesboat | EasyPost | | AwokenLazarus | @AwokenLazarus | | | Crocopaco | @DaBlitzStein | | | Keran McKenzie | @keranm | | | Ventz Petkov | @ventz | | | Mat Balez | @matbalez | | ### Leadership Team & Decision Process Mic is project creator, and works with: | James Dumay | @i386 | General Inference | | Michael Neale | @michaelneale / @micspiral | Spiral (Block) | | Nick DiZazzo | @ndizazzo | tetrate | | Daniel Winter-Wijntjes | @danielwinterw | General Inference | as persistent community that help decide directions, but happens in the weekly meeting or public chat. There is a lot of support from others such as | Steven Mih | @StevenMih | Action State Group | | Virgile Pourchet | @Virgile-pct | | who provide additional leadership around platforms (eg windows) ### Lifecycle Stage Evidence Sandbox: Meshllm is a project to allow people to pool compute (all hardware and operating system platforms) in a safe way so that it can be consumed via a standard api from standard and familiar tools (chat, harnesses, apps and more), making use of this hardware. It benefits from public adoption for public mesh sharing (which is more an exemplar use case) but also for wide platform support (which arouse out of community). Anyone using an agent or chat could make use of this, developers via the SDK to end consumers via an app. roadmap: https://github.com/Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm/blob/main/ROADMAP.md ### Security we make use of https://github.com/project-loupe/loupe which scans the core repo and others and opens issues which are agentically addressed as the project progresses (and veing agent driven upgrades tend to happen frequently of dependencies). https://github.com/Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm/blob/main/SECURITY.md ### Website URL https://meshllm.cloud/ ### Documented Governance Practices (if any) early stage - see governance model section above. ### Links to Social Media Accounts https://x.com/Mesh_LLM, https://www.linkedin.com/groups/40937000/ (neither heavily used) ### Trademark and accounts - [x] If the project is accepted, I agree to transfer all project trademarks and accounts to the Linux Foundation under the contribution agreement. ### Details of Existing Financial Sponsorship _No response_ ### Infrastructure Needs or Requests TBD ### Additional Information _No response_ ### Application contact name(s) and email(s) michael.neale@gmail.com, mat@spiral.xyz, steve@spiral.xyz, nidhi@squareup.com ### Contributing or sponsoring entity signatory information If an organization: | Name | Address | Type (e.g., Delaware corporation) | Signatory name and title | Email address | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------| | Block | 1955 Broadway, Suite 600 Oakland, CA 94612, United States | Delaware Corp | nidhi | nidhi@squareup.com | Or, if an individual or individual(s): | Name | Country | Email address | |-----------|-----------|-----------| | Mic Neale | Australia | michael.neale@gmail.com | | | | | | | | |
